newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean new foreign investment up 22 pct Jan-April.
newsitem.headline: Chilean new foreign investment up 22 pct Jan-April.

text.p: New foreign investment in Chile rose 22 percent in the first four months of the year over the same period of 1996, to $1.9 billion, the government's Foreign Investment Committee said Tuesday.
The sharpest increase was in investment through American Depositary Receipts, which climbed 55 percent to $625 million, the committee said in a report.
Investment through Decree Law 600, which authorizes direct investment, rose a more modest 7.7 percent in the first four months of the year, to $1.1 billion, it said.
The mining sector accounted for 58 percent of the direct investment, followed by service industries with 20 percent and the industrial sector with 18 percent.
Investment under Central Bank Chapter 14 rules governing loans to existing projects totalled $137 million.
The figures showed Chile authorized foreign investment worth $3.6 billion in the first four months of the year, up a steep 135 percent from the same period of 1996.

This includes approval of a $2.75 billion investment to expand the Los Pelambres copper mine, requested by English firm Los Pelambres Investment Co Ltd and Dutch-registered companies Nippon LP Resources BV and MM LP Holding BV.

Other projects include a $15 million investment by Caterpillar Inc's Caterpillar Financial Services Corp to set up a division in Chile to import Caterpillar products to Latin America's Southern Cone region.
